_comment: Tier-2 fixture for poisson pitfall #0: 'Must call triangulation.refine_global() before distributing DOFs. Calling distribute_dofs on a 1-cell triangulation runs but gives a useless 4-DoF system. Signal: SolverControl reports Convergence step 0 value... dof_handler.n_dofs() returns 4.' We verify the n_dofs() returns the small value as predicted.MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. The T2_MUTATE=1 hook is left in source.cpp so the negative result stays re-runnable, but NO _mutation recipe is declared: a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding it is (same treatment as dune/point_indicator_selects_no_facet and febio/static_activation_ramp_shape_does_not_matter). Re-run by hand from the fixture directory after any harness run has built it: `T2_MUTATE=1 ./_build/prog`. The hook calls tria.refine_global(3) — precisely the call this pitfall is about forgetting. Measured 2026-08-07: n_dofs goes from 4 to 81, the program prints "FIXTURE WARNING: n_dofs is 81, not 4" and exits 2, and the fixture STILL PASSES. The reason is structural: expect_in_output is ["n_dofs", "DoFHandler"] and both strings live in the line "DoFHandler::n_dofs() = <value>", which is printed whatever the value is. The number 4 — the entire content of the pitfall — is asserted only inside the C++, and mode compile_and_run ignores the exit code and greps stdout, so the harness never sees that assertion fail. The fix would be an expectation naming the measured value; it is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a mutation control stops being evidence.
